hops.title: Read the back of a vending-machine bestseller
hops.text: Next time you pass a vending machine, turn the bestsellers over and read the panels: peanut-butter crackers, cheese chips, frosted pastries. Many stack fat and carbohydrate in the same bite. In 2018, DiFeliceantonio and colleagues ran a real-money snack auction inside a brain scanner. For snacks matched on average for calories, liking and familiarity, people bid more for combinations than for snacks mainly rich in fat or in carbohydrate, and signals in reward-related brain regions tracked the bids. A 2021 auction found healthy-weight participants bidding more for combinations than for mostly carbohydrate snacks, and no clear effect of snack category in participants with overweight or obesity.

sources.citation: DiFeliceantonio AG et al. Supra-additive effects of combining fat and carbohydrate on food reward. Cell Metab (2018).
Perszyk EE et al. Fat and carbohydrate interactions and food reward. Nutrients (2021).

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A student standing by a campus vending machine examining the back of a snack package.
image.caption: Healthy-weight volunteers bid more for fat-plus-carbohydrate snacks than for snacks mainly rich in carbohydrate.

hops.afterHeading: GLP-1: three routes, not one relay
hops.title: The Gila monster venom behind the GLP-1 drugs
hops.text: Active GLP-1 from gut L cells has a blood half-life of one to two minutes, partly because an enzyme clips its front end, and that made it a frustrating drug. Separately, looking for a peptide similar to exendin-3, already known from a related lizard, John Eng's team screened Gila monster venom and found exendin-4. It shares GLP-1's first amino acid and resists that clipping. As immediate-release exenatide, it has a mean terminal half-life of about 2.4 hours and became the first approved GLP-1 receptor agonist; semaglutide came by another route, a stabilized GLP-1. A drug that circulates much longer can act in places gut GLP-1 may never reach.

sources.citation: Friedman JM. The discovery and development of GLP-1 based therapeutics. PNAS (2024).
Muller TD et al. Glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1). Mol Metab (2019).
Byetta (exenatide) prescribing information, section 12.3 (mean terminal half-life 2.4 h). FDA (2025).
Eng J et al. Isolation and characterization of exendin-4, an exendin-3 analogue, from Heloderma suspectum venom. J Biol Chem (1992).

hops.afterHeading: Sugar without taste: exact genotypes and cell types
hops.title: How oral rehydration works in cholera
hops.text: Cholera can make the intestine lose water and salts faster than the body can replace them. In August 1960, Robert Crane brought a sketch to a Prague meeting: one carrier in intestinal cells moves sodium and glucose together. That carrier is SGLT1, the transporter mice need for the vagal response to intestinal sucrose, and it keeps working while the intestine secretes salts and water. Oral rehydration solution pairs glucose and electrolytes in measured proportions, letting SGLT1 absorb sodium and glucose together as water follows. In 1978 The Lancet called that coupling potentially the century's most important medical advance. Oral rehydration still saves millions of lives a year.

sources.citation: Hamilton KL. Robert K. Crane - Na+-glucose cotransporter to cure? Front Physiol (2013).
